--- title: "Seasonal space use" subtitle: "East Alligator" author: "Scott Forrest" date: "2026-11-06" execute: cache: false warning: false bibliography: paperpile.bib toc: true number-sections: false format: html: self-contained: false code-fold: true code-summary: "Show code" code-tools: true df-print: paged code-line-numbers: true code-overflow: scroll fig-format: png fig-dpi: 300 pdf: fig-format: png fig-dpi: 300 geometry: - top=30mm - left=30mm editor: source abstract: | Quantifying the space use of the pigs in East Alligator, and how that changes across seasons and for different months of the year. For estimating space use we are using 'occurrence' distributions, which are the probability of finding an animal in a given area at a given time. This is different to 'range' distributions, which are the probability of finding an animal in a given area over a long period of time (i.e. their home range). Occurrence distributions are more appropriate for short-term space use, such as across seasons and months. --- # Load packages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) packages <- c("amt", "lubridate", "ctmm", "terra", "sf", "beepr", "tictoc", "leaflet", "viridis") walk(packages, require, character.only = T) # prevent scientific notation in outputs options(scipen = 999) ``` ::: # Create directories for outputs ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # general outputs directory outputs_dir <- "outputs/east_alligator/space_use/" dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE) ``` ::: # Import GPS tracking data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pig_all_steps <- read_csv("data/pigs_east_alligator_steps_covs_20261015.csv") # Convert timezone after import (resets to UTC) pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% mutate( t1_ = with_tz(t1_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin"), t2_ = with_tz(t2_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin") ) ``` ::: ## Get into format for ctmm ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # keep relevant columns pig_all <- pig_all_steps %>% dplyr::select(name, t1_, x1_, y1_, date, month, season) head(pig_all) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Select a subset of the data for prototyping ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pig_subset <- pig_all %>% filter(month == 11) # choose which dataset to use # pig_data <- pig_subset pig_data <- pig_all ``` ::: ## Convert to ctmm telemetry object ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # as.telemetry() identifies columns by their Movebank names, so we rename them. # x1_/y1_ are in GDA94 / GA Lambert (EPSG:3112), so convert to WGS84 lon/lat pig_data_movebank <- pig_data %>% filter(!is.na(x1_), !is.na(y1_), !is.na(t1_)) %>% st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112, remove = FALSE) %>% st_transform(crs = 4326) %>% mutate(location.long = st_coordinates(.)[, 1], location.lat = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% transmute(ID = name, timestamp = t1_, location.long, location.lat, month, season) %>% as.data.frame() # returns a list of telemetry objects, one per individual pig_data_ctmm <- as.telemetry(pig_data_movebank, timezone = "Australia/Darwin", keep = c("month", "season")) ``` ::: # Pull out one pig for visualisation and testing I am using the tutorial at to estimate home ranges over the full tracking period. ## Betty ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pig_betty <- pig_data_ctmm[["Betty"]] plot(pig_betty) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](space_use_east_alligator_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png) ::: ::: ## Check range residency We can see that Betty's variogram is asymptotic after a very short period, indicating that she is range resident. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} level <- 0.95 # we want to display 95% confidence intervals xlim <- c(0,2 %#% "month") # to create a window of 2 months SVF <- variogram(pig_betty) par(mfrow = c(1,2)) plot(SVF, fraction = 1, level = level) # abline(v = 0.1, col = "red", lty = 2) # adding a line at 1 month plot(SVF, xlim = xlim, level = level) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](space_use_east_alligator_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png) ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # abline(v = 0.1, col = "red", lty = 2) ``` ::: ## Selecting a movement model ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Calculate an automated model guesstimate: GUESS1 <- ctmm.guess(pig_betty, interactive = FALSE) # Automated model selection, starting from GUESS: FIT1_ML <- ctmm.select(pig_betty, GUESS1, method = 'ML') FIT1_pHREML <- ctmm.select(pig_betty, GUESS1, method = 'pHREML') ## reminder: it will default to pHREML if no method is specified. summary(FIT1_ML) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $name [1] "OUF anisotropic" $DOF mean area diffusion speed 170.2003 324.4206 2127.6033 3521.4392 $CI low est high area (square kilometers) 3.773547 4.220346 4.691783 τ[position] (hours) 8.349614 9.401327 10.585513 τ[velocity] (minutes) 15.834915 16.683553 17.577673 speed (kilometers/day) 11.475812 11.668526 11.861196 diffusion (square kilometers/day) 1.357282 1.416853 1.477685 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} summary(FIT1_pHREML) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $name [1] "OUF anisotropic" $DOF mean area diffusion speed 169.1766 318.9748 2126.5882 3521.2704 $CI low est high area (square kilometers) 3.792260 4.245427 4.723801 τ[position] (hours) 8.393667 9.460375 10.662645 τ[velocity] (minutes) 15.828221 16.676445 17.570125 speed (kilometers/day) 11.475839 11.668559 11.861234 diffusion (square kilometers/day) 1.357422 1.417014 1.477868 ``` ::: ::: ### Checking model selection ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} FIT1_pHREML_verbose <- ctmm.select(pig_betty, GUESS1, verbose = TRUE) summary(FIT1_pHREML_verbose) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ΔAICc ΔRMSPE (m) DOF[area] OUF anisotropic 0.000 104.0771 318.9748 OU anisotropic 1694.891 115.4375 194.1613 OUf anisotropic 1735.407 0.0000 1184.5374 OUF 3929.182 245.5171 304.3702 ``` ::: ::: ## Providing a movement model to the home range estimator ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Run an area-corrected AKDE: UD1_ML <- akde(pig_betty, FIT1_ML) UD1_pHREML <- akde(pig_betty, FIT1_pHREML) summary(UD1_pHREML)$CI # home range area estimation ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` low est high area (square kilometers) 2.266867 2.537752 2.823706 ``` ::: ::: ## Diagnostics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(UD1_pHREML)$DOF["area"] # effective sample size of Betty ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` area 318.9748 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} nrow(pig_betty) # absolute sample size ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 6498 ``` ::: ::: ## Weighted AKDE for comparison ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} UD1w_pHREML <- akde(pig_betty, FIT1_pHREML, weights = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](space_use_east_alligator_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png) ::: ```{.r .cell-code} summary(UD1w_pHREML)$CI # home range area estimation (weighted) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` low est high area (square kilometers) 2.257367 2.527118 2.811873 ``` ::: ::: ## Plotting estimated home ranges ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Creating an extent that includes both UDs at the 95% CI level: EXT <- extent(list(UD1_ML, UD1_pHREML, UD1w_pHREML), level = 0.95) # Plotting pHREML (with and without weights) side-by-side: par(mfrow = c(1,2)) plot(pig_betty, UD = UD1_pHREML, ext = EXT) title(expression("pHREML AKDE"["C"])) plot(pig_betty, UD = UD1w_pHREML, ext = EXT) title(expression("pHREML wAKDE"["C"])) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](space_use_east_alligator_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png) ::: ::: # All pigs ## Nest the telemetry objects One row per pig, with the telemetry object in a list column. The movement models and home ranges are then added as further list columns. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pigs_nested <- tibble(name = names(pig_data_ctmm), telemetry = pig_data_ctmm) pigs_nested ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Fit movement models and estimate home ranges Model selection is slow, so the results are saved and re-loaded if they already exist. Delete the file to re-fit. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} hr_fits_file <- paste0(outputs_dir, "pigs_nested_akde.rds") if (file.exists(hr_fits_file)) { pigs_nested <- readRDS(hr_fits_file) } else { tic() pigs_nested <- pigs_nested %>% mutate( # automated model guesstimate guess = map(telemetry, ~ ctmm.guess(.x, interactive = FALSE)), # model selection (defaults to pHREML) fit = map2(telemetry, guess, ~ ctmm.select(.x, .y)), # area-corrected AKDE ud = map2(telemetry, fit, ~ akde(.x, .y)) ) toc() saveRDS(pigs_nested, hr_fits_file) beep(sound = 2) } ``` ::: ## Summarise the models and home range areas ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pigs_hr_summary <- pigs_nested %>% mutate( n_locations = map_int(telemetry, nrow), model = map_chr(fit, ~ summary(.x)$name), DOF_area = map_dbl(ud, ~ summary(.x)$DOF["area"]), # 95% home range area and CIs (units are reported in the column name) hr_area = map(ud, ~ { CI <- summary(.x)$CI tibble(units = rownames(CI), low = CI[1, "low"], est = CI[1, "est"], high = CI[1, "high"]) }) ) %>% dplyr::select(name, n_locations, model, DOF_area, hr_area) %>% unnest(hr_area) pigs_hr_summary ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} write_csv(pigs_hr_summary, paste0(outputs_dir, "pigs_hr_summary.csv")) ``` ::: ## Plot the home ranges ### Individually with ctmm ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pwalk(list(pigs_nested$name, pigs_nested$telemetry, pigs_nested$ud), function(name, telemetry, ud) { plot(telemetry, UD = ud) title(name) }) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} and save for QGIS `as.sf()` returns three polygons per pig for each contour level - the lower CI, the estimate and the upper CI. We extract the 50% (core area) and 95% (home range) contours. Each UD is in ctmm's own local projection, so they are all transformed to EPSG:3112 to match the rest of the data. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # home range contours to extract contour_levels <- c(0.5, 0.95) pigs_hr_sf <- pigs_nested %>% dplyr::select(name, ud) %>% # one row per pig per contour level crossing(level_ud = contour_levels) %>% mutate(hr_sf = map2(ud, level_ud, ~ as.sf(.x, level.UD = .y, level = 0.95) %>% st_transform(crs = 3112))) %>% dplyr::select(name, level_ud, hr_sf) %>% # as.sf already has a 'name' column (e.g. "Betty 95% est"), so rename it mutate(hr_sf = map(hr_sf, ~ rename(.x, contour = name))) %>% unnest(hr_sf) %>% mutate(ci = word(contour, -1)) %>% st_as_sf(crs = 3112) pigs_hr_sf ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # a single GeoPackage with all pigs (filter on 'level_ud' and 'ci' in QGIS) st_write(pigs_hr_sf, paste0(outputs_dir, "pigs_hr_akde.gpkg"), delete_dsn = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Deleting source `outputs/east_alligator/space_use/pigs_hr_akde.gpkg' using driver `GPKG' Writing layer `pigs_hr_akde' to data source `outputs/east_alligator/space_use/pigs_hr_akde.gpkg' using driver `GPKG' Writing 114 features with 4 fields and geometry type Unknown (any). ``` ::: ::: ### All pigs together ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pigs_hr_sf %>% filter(ci == "est") %>% ggplot() + geom_point(data = pig_data, aes(x = x1_, y = y1_, colour = name), alpha = 0.1, size = 0.25) + # point estimates of the 50% (dashed) and 95% (solid) contours geom_sf(aes(colour = name, linetype = factor(level_ud)), fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5) + scale_colour_viridis_d(guide = "none") + scale_linetype_manual("Contour", values = c("0.5" = "dashed", "0.95" = "solid"), labels = c("50%", "95%")) + coord_sf(datum = 3112) + labs(title = "50% and 95% AKDE home ranges", x = "", y = "") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](space_use_east_alligator_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png) ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ggsave(paste0(outputs_dir, "pigs_hr_akde.png"), width = 150, height = 150, units = "mm", scale = 1.25, dpi = 600) ``` ::: ## Plot interactively with leaflet Each contour level is a separate layer that can be toggled in the layers control. The CIs and GPS fixes are hidden by default. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # reproject to WGS84 (EPSG:4326) for leaflet, and add the contour area pigs_hr_sf_wgs84 <- pigs_hr_sf %>% mutate(area_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(.)) / 1e6) %>% st_transform(crs = 4326) %>% mutate(popup = paste0("ID: ", name, "
Contour: ", level_ud * 100, "% (", ci, ")", "
Area: ", round(area_km2, 2), " km2")) hr_50_est <- pigs_hr_sf_wgs84 %>% filter(level_ud == 0.5, ci == "est") hr_95_est <- pigs_hr_sf_wgs84 %>% filter(level_ud == 0.95, ci == "est") hr_95_ci <- pigs_hr_sf_wgs84 %>% filter(level_ud == 0.95, ci != "est") # GPS fixes (x1_/y1_ are in GDA94 / GA Lambert, EPSG:3112) pig_map_pts <- pig_data %>% filter(!is.na(x1_), !is.na(y1_)) %>% st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112) %>% st_transform(crs = 4326) pal <- colorFactor(viridisLite::viridis(n_distinct(pigs_hr_sf_wgs84$name), option = "H"), domain = pigs_hr_sf_wgs84$name) hr_map <- leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>% addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>% addPolygons(data = hr_95_est, color = ~ pal(name), weight = 2, opacity = 1, fillColor = ~ pal(name), fillOpacity = 0.15, popup = ~ popup, highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 4, bringToFront = TRUE), group = "95% home range") %>% addPolygons(data = hr_50_est, color = ~ pal(name), weight = 2, opacity = 1, fillColor = ~ pal(name), fillOpacity = 0.35, popup = ~ popup, highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 4, bringToFront = TRUE), group = "50% core area") %>% addPolylines(data = hr_95_ci, color = ~ pal(name), weight = 1, opacity = 0.8, dashArray = "4 4", popup = ~ popup, group = "95% CIs") %>% # WebGL points, as there can be a lot of fixes leafgl::addGlPoints(data = pig_map_pts, fillColor = pal(pig_map_pts$name), fillOpacity = 0.75, radius = 4, popup = paste0("ID: ", pig_map_pts$name, "
Time: ", pig_map_pts$t1_), group = "GPS fixes") %>% addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal, values = pigs_hr_sf_wgs84$name, title = "Pig ID") %>% addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft", options = scaleBarOptions(imperial = FALSE)) %>% addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("95% home range", "50% core area", "95% CIs", "GPS fixes"), options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) %>% hideGroup(c("95% CIs", "GPS fixes")) # save a standalone copy to open in the browser (or share) htmlwidgets::saveWidget(hr_map, file.path(outputs_dir, "pigs_hr_akde_map.html"), selfcontained = TRUE) # Embedding the maps inline makes the rendered page (and its _freeze file) # too large for GitHub, so when rendering, the saved map is shown in an iframe # instead (_quarto.yml copies outputs/**/*.html into the site). When working # interactively the map is shown in the viewer as usual. embed_map <- function(map, filename, height = 600) { if (interactive()) return(map) htmltools::tags$iframe(src = paste0(outputs_dir, filename), width = "100%", height = height, style = "border: none;") } embed_map(hr_map, "pigs_hr_akde_map.html") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: # Monthly space use Here we estimate space use separately for each pig in each calendar month, keeping the same month in different years separate (e.g. October 2025 and October 2026). This uses all of the data (`pig_all`) rather than the prototyping subset. ## Settings Pig-months with only a few days of data (e.g. when the collar was deployed or dropped off part-way through a month) will have artificially small areas, so they are removed. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # minimum number of days with fixes for a pig-month to be included min_days <- 20 # contour levels (50% core area and 95% home range) contour_levels <- c(0.5, 0.95) # set to a number to only fit the first n pig-months with ctmm (for testing), # or NA to fit them all n_test <- NA ``` ::: ## Split the data into pig-months ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pig_monthly <- pig_all %>% filter(!is.na(x1_), !is.na(y1_), !is.na(t1_)) %>% mutate(year_month = format(t1_, "%Y-%m"), month_date = floor_date(as_date(t1_), "month")) %>% nest(data = -c(name, year_month, month_date)) %>% mutate(n_fixes = map_int(data, nrow), n_days = map_int(data, ~ n_distinct(as_date(.x$t1_)))) %>% arrange(name, month_date) # pig-months that are removed pig_monthly %>% filter(n_days < min_days) %>% dplyr::select(-data) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} pig_monthly <- pig_monthly %>% filter(n_days >= min_days) # number of pig-months for each month pig_monthly %>% count(month_date) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Using MCP Minimum convex polygons from the `amt` package. The 95% MCP excludes the 5% of fixes furthest from the centroid. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} hr_monthly_mcp_sf <- pig_monthly %>% mutate(track = map(data, ~ make_track(.x, x1_, y1_, t1_, crs = 3112)), mcp_sf = map(track, ~ hr_mcp(.x, levels = contour_levels) %>% hr_isopleths())) %>% dplyr::select(name, year_month, month_date, mcp_sf) %>% unnest(mcp_sf) %>% st_as_sf(crs = 3112) %>% mutate(method = "MCP", level_ud = level, ci = "est", area_km2 = as.numeric(area) / 1e6) %>% dplyr::select(name, year_month, month_date, method, level_ud, ci, area_km2) hr_monthly_mcp_sf ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Using ctmm Kriging estimates For each pig-month we fit a movement model (pHREML) and then estimate the occurrence distribution with `occurrence()`, which uses time-series Kriging to estimate where the pig was during the sampling period. Since we already have the movement model, we also estimate the monthly AKDE home range (which estimates the range the pig would use in the long run if it continued to behave as it did that month). The model type of each pig (e.g. OUF anisotropic) is taken from the model selected for that pig above (`pigs_nested$fit`), so the same type is used for every month of a pig. The parameters (e.g. the range and the positional and velocity autocorrelation time scales) are still estimated separately for each month, as movement rates differ between seasons. This is faster and more stable than running model selection for each pig-month. Pigs without a fit above fall back to model selection for each month. The model types above should be selected from the full tracking period, i.e. with `pig_data <- pig_all` when the 'All pigs' section is run. Note that the area of the occurrence distribution is not a home range area. It represents the uncertainty in the pig's path, so it depends on the sampling rate (which is the same across all pigs here, so comparisons between pigs and months are still valid). Model fitting is slow, so this runs in parallel and the results are saved and re-loaded if they already exist. Delete the file to re-fit. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # convert one pig-month of data to a ctmm telemetry object # (as.telemetry() identifies columns by their Movebank names, and x1_/y1_ # are in GDA94 / GA Lambert, EPSG:3112) to_telemetry <- function(df, id) { df %>% st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112) %>% st_transform(crs = 4326) %>% mutate(location.long = st_coordinates(.)[, 1], location.lat = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% transmute(ID = id, timestamp = t1_, location.long, location.lat) %>% as.data.frame() %>% as.telemetry(timezone = "Australia/Darwin") %>% suppressMessages() } # fit the movement model and return the occurrence and AKDE contours as sf # (in EPSG:3112). The UD rasters themselves are not kept to save memory. # pig_fit is the model selected for that pig over the full tracking period, # which sets the model type. The parameters are estimated from the month's data. fit_monthly_ctmm <- function(tel, pig_fit, levels) { if (is.null(pig_fit)) { guess <- ctmm.guess(tel, interactive = FALSE) fit <- ctmm.select(tel, guess) } else { # the guess takes the model structure from pig_fit, and its parameters as # starting values (the mean location is re-estimated), which are then # all re-estimated from this month's data guess <- ctmm.guess(tel, CTMM = pig_fit, interactive = FALSE) fit <- ctmm.fit(tel, guess, method = "pHREML") } od <- occurrence(tel, fit) ud <- akde(tel, fit) # as.sf() has a 'name' column (e.g. "Betty 95% est") contours <- function(x, method) { lapply(levels, function(l) { s <- sf::st_transform(as.sf(x, level.UD = l, level = 0.95), crs = 3112) s$level_ud <- l s$method <- method s }) %>% do.call(rbind, .) } list(fit = fit, contours = rbind(contours(od, "Occurrence (Kriging)"), contours(ud, "AKDE"))) } hr_monthly_ctmm_file <- paste0(outputs_dir, "pig_monthly_ctmm.rds") if (file.exists(hr_monthly_ctmm_file)) { pig_monthly_ctmm <- readRDS(hr_monthly_ctmm_file) } else { pig_monthly_ctmm <- pig_monthly %>% dplyr::select(name, year_month, month_date, data) %>% { if (is.na(n_test)) . else slice_head(., n = n_test) } %>% mutate(telemetry = map2(data, name, to_telemetry)) %>% # model selected for each pig above (NULL for pigs without one) left_join(pigs_nested %>% dplyr::select(name, pig_fit = fit), by = "name") tic() future::plan(future::multisession, workers = max(1, parallelly::availableCores() - 2)) pig_monthly_ctmm <- pig_monthly_ctmm %>% mutate(ctmm = furrr::future_map2( telemetry, pig_fit, # a failed fit returns NULL rather than stopping the whole loop possibly(~ fit_monthly_ctmm(.x, .y, contour_levels), otherwise = NULL), .options = furrr::furrr_options(seed = TRUE, packages = c("ctmm", "sf")), .progress = TRUE)) future::plan(future::sequential) toc() pig_monthly_ctmm <- pig_monthly_ctmm %>% dplyr::select(-data, -pig_fit) saveRDS(pig_monthly_ctmm, hr_monthly_ctmm_file) beep() } # any pig-months where the fit failed pig_monthly_ctmm %>% filter(map_lgl(ctmm, is.null)) %>% dplyr::select(name, year_month) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
